title: Budget-matched dense scene-coordinate consensus: receptive-field trunk, warm-started votes, annealed-scale IRLS
hypothesis: exp-55 already built a faithful ACE/DSAC-style measurement of this exact forced family -- from-scratch trunk, shared 1x1-conv per-cell head over a 16x16 grid, 4-rotation fan (1,024 votes), 3-round differentiable Geman-McClure IRLS consensus -- and lost badly (2360.39 m vs champion's 1176.5 m) at the SAME light training budget (1,500 crops/bucket, 9 total epochs) the current champion reference itself uses. So the family wasn't handicapped by an unfair budget relative to champion; but it also never had a REAL budget in absolute terms, and this design has three structural reasons a real budget specifically helps it where it can't help a shallow/mistuned version of the same mechanism: (1) each of the trunk's three stride-2 stages plus one stride-1 refinement gives a receptive field of only ~20px out of a 128px crop -- every one of the 1,024 votes is guessing a location from a small, close-up texture patch with no sense of where that patch sits in the wider scene, which more optimizer steps cannot fix because it's a capacity/architecture ceiling, not a convergence gap; (2) the IRLS redescending kernel used ONE FIXED scale from step zero, so early in training -- when all 1,024 per-cell heads are still near-random -- the kernel had no legitimate signal to separate inlier votes from noise and could lock onto an arbitrary early subset that more of the SAME fixed-scale training cannot escape, since scale never adapts to how trustworthy the votes currently are; (3) the heteroscedastic per-vote NLL term was live from step zero, when raw errors are enormous and near-uniform across cells, a regime where minimizing that loss is often cheaper by inflating predicted log-variance than by improving the mean prediction, which can quietly stall exactly the mean-accuracy learning a longer budget is supposed to buy. This experiment keeps the forced family's structure intact but replaces the trunk's receptive field, the IRLS scale schedule, and the loss curriculum with versions that are specifically built to keep improving as optimizer steps increase, instead of just being the same fixed-hyperparameter design run for longer.
method: In model/model.py: (1) grow the from-scratch trunk's receptive field via a stride-1 dilated-conv refinement block (dilations 2 then 4, 128ch) appended after the existing stride-8 stem, before the shared 1x1-conv per-cell head -- widening every cell's effective field of view toward the whole 128x128 crop instead of a ~20px patch, so cell content carries scene-level context, not just local texture; (2) replace the per-cell head's default init with an explicit warm start (zero weight, bias fixed so every vote starts at map-center (u=v=0.5) with a wide initial log-sigma) so untrained/early-trained votes sit at the same bounded-floor default every kept model in this project's history has relied on, instead of scattering randomly before IRLS has anything coherent to reweight; (3) add a per-rotation learned reliability scale (4 softplus-positive scalars, one per C4 turn) that multiplies each turn's 256 votes' initial IRLS weight, since a from-scratch trunk has no built-in rotation-equivariance guarantee that all 4 passes are equally trustworthy; (4) replace the IRLS kernel's fixed scale constant with a registered buffer (model.irls_scale) that model/train.py anneals geometrically from loose (0.25 normalized uv units) to tight (0.05, matching GOOD_ERR_UV) across the training run, fixed at its final tight value for calibration/export -- so early steps behave close to a stable soft mean over all votes (nothing is confidently thrown out before the heads know anything) and only later steps sharpen into genuine outlier rejection. In model/train.py: (5) add a loss warm-up -- the first 15% of total optimizer steps use plain per-vote L2 + consensus L2 only (heteroscedastic NLL and confidence-BCE weight at zero), and the schedule steps model.irls_scale down over the SAME progress fraction each step, before the remaining 85% turn on the full per-vote heteroscedastic NLL + confidence BCE terms at their normal weights, matched exactly to the schedule step already driving the cosine LR anneal, so no new step-counting logic; (6) rebuild the confusability-weighted training sampler at the individual-location level (nearest-distant-location descriptor match, replacing the current committed compute_cell_weights which is still tied to the now-deleted 1024-cell classifier grid); (7) bump EPOCH_MULT from 3 to 6 so this design cashes in a real optimizer-step budget as more effective epochs regardless of whatever --epochs the harness invocation passes this round, since the whole point of this design is to test whether the family benefits from real budget rather than just asserting it will.
expected_outcome: If receptive-field starvation and a static, un-annealed IRLS/loss schedule were the dominant reasons exp-55 lost by ~2x under a training budget genuinely large enough to let a from-scratch trunk converge, this design should land meaningfully closer to or below champion's 1176.5 m -- a result in the 600-1200 m range would support that reading. A result still in the 2000+ m range despite the added budget, receptive field, warm start, and curriculum would be a third clean measurement (after exp-4's plain mean and exp-55's fixed-scale IRLS) that the dense-per-patch-consensus family is refuted at the family level for this project's single-crop-center supervision, not merely under-optimized -- and should redirect future rounds toward global-descriptor families instead of further tuning this one's aggregator.
eli5: Picture a search team where 1,024 people each look at a tiny postage-stamp-sized patch of a photo and guess 'this is roughly here on the map,' and then the team averages the guesses, throwing out the wildest outliers as they go. Last time we tried this, each searcher's postage stamp was so small and close-up they barely knew what part of town they were even looking at, and the 'throw out the wildest guesses' rule used one fixed strictness the whole time -- too strict before anyone had learned anything useful, which can accidentally lock the team onto a bad early answer forever. This time, each searcher gets a wider window to look through, everyone starts by guessing 'probably the middle of the map' until they've actually learned something, and the strictness for throwing out bad guesses starts loose and only tightens up gradually as training goes on -- so the team can't get stuck early, and the extra training time we're giving it this round actually has a chance to pay off.

stages.name: Camera frame
stages.detail: 128x128 px aerial crop, one of 6 simulated lighting conditions

stages.name: From-scratch spatial trunk
stages.detail: a from-scratch conv stack (three stride-2 stages, 32->64->96 channels, stride 8 total) turns the 128x128 photo into a 16x16 grid of local feature vectors, then a stride-1 dilated-conv refinement block (dilations 2 and 4, 128 channels) widens every cell's view of the surrounding scene before handing off to the per-cell voters -- so each of the 16x16 spots knows roughly what part of the wider photo it sits in, not just its own close-up patch

stages.name: Rotation-vote pool
stages.detail: the photo's four 90-degree turns each get their own full pass through the trunk (4x16x16 = 1,024 independent local glimpses); a small learned per-turn trust score now also scales how much weight each turn's 256 glimpses start with in the consensus below, since nothing guarantees a from-scratch trunk treats all four turns equally reliably

stages.name: Per-cell coordinate voters
stages.detail: a single shared small head reads each of the 1,024 local glimpses and guesses its own (map-x, map-y) coordinate plus how sure it is -- now warm-started so every vote begins at the safe map-center guess with wide uncertainty, rather than a random scattered guess, before training has taught it anything

stages.name: Robust consensus solve
stages.detail: the 1,024 guesses are combined by repeated re-weighting: start from a confidence-weighted average, then run three rounds where guesses far from the emerging group answer get turned down and the average is recomputed. The strictness of 'how far is too far' now starts loose (barely rejects anything) and gradually tightens over the course of training, instead of being fixed from the very first step -- so the team isn't asked to make sharp judgment calls before it has anything worth judging

stages.name: Confidence
stages.detail: reads how tightly the surviving votes clustered by the end of the re-weighting plus how far apart they still are; unchanged mechanism, now fed by the receptive-field-widened trunk and the per-turn trust scores above it

stages.name: Training data
stages.detail: the confusability oversampling idea is rebuilt at the level of individual training locations (nearest-distant-location descriptor match) instead of the now-deleted 1,024-cell classifier grid the currently-committed code still keys off of -- same look-alike-places-drawn-more-often idea, recomputed for this design's decode

stages.name: Training signal
stages.detail: the first 15% of training grades every vote and the final consensus answer with a plain distance-squared penalty only; the remaining 85% adds the full grading (wrong-and-overconfident penalized harder than wrong-and-uncertain, plus the confidence-hit signal), so the model isn't asked to calibrate its own uncertainty before its guesses are even in the right neighborhood

stages.name: Training schedule
stages.detail: one shared learning-rate glide for the whole network, now run for roughly twice as many effective passes over the training data as the last IRLS attempt got, so this design actually gets the real training budget its hypothesis depends on

implementation_brief:
Restate the fixed contracts first: train.py's CLI (--area, --out-dir, --data-dir, --epochs, --max-crops-per-bucket, --seed) must not change, and model.py's ONNX export contract (1x3x128x128 float32 [0,1] input named 'frame' -> output named 'uvc', a single [1,3] tensor of (u, v, conf) with u,v normalized map coords in [0,1] and conf in [0,1]) must be preserved exactly -- the frozen scorer (pipeline/score.py) depends on both.

model/model.py -- full rewrite of TinyLocNet and its module-level constants (no mobilenet_v3_small import, no PRETRAINED_TRUNK_PATH, no GRID_K classifier field left anywhere):
- Trunk: nn.Sequential of 3 stride-2 conv blocks (Conv2d+BatchNorm2d+ReLU), channels 3->32->64->96, kernel 3, producing a 16x16x96 feature map from a 128x128x3 input (verify with a probe forward pass, matching the existing _build_pretrained_trunk probe pattern). Append a refinement block of 2 residual dilated conv layers (Conv2d(96 or 128, 128, kernel 3, dilation=2, padding=2) then Conv2d(128, 128, kernel 3, dilation=4, padding=4), each BatchNorm2d+ReLU, stride 1 throughout so spatial size stays 16x16) -> final per-cell feature width FEAT_CH=128.
- C4 rotation stack: keep _c4_stack exactly as-is (transpose+flip based, [N,3,H,W] -> [4N,3,H,W]).
- Per-cell voter head: nn.Conv2d(FEAT_CH, 3, kernel_size=1) applied to the 4N x FEAT_CH x 16 x 16 feature map, producing 4N x 3 x 16 x 16 (channels = u, v, log_sigma per cell). Warm start: initialize this conv's weight to zero (nn.init.zeros_) and bias to [0.5, 0.5, log(0.2)] so every vote starts at map-center with log_sigma=log(0.2) (wide/uncertain) before any training. Flatten spatial dims to get, per rotation-major batch element, 256 per-cell (u,v,log_sigma) votes; reshape across the 4 rotation copies to get 1,024 votes per original crop, tagging each with its rotation index r in 0..3.
- Per-rotation reliability: a single nn.Parameter of shape [4] (init 0.0), passed through softplus, broadcast-multiplied into each rotation's 256 votes' initial IRLS weight (see below) -- this is the ONLY use of rotation identity; nothing else about the votes depends on which turn produced them.
- IRLS consensus: register a buffer self.irls_scale = torch.tensor(0.25) (module-level constant IRLS_SCALE_START = 0.25, IRLS_SCALE_END = 0.05 for reference/reset). Initial weight per vote: w0 = softplus(rot_reliability[r]) * exp(-log_sigma) (equivalently 1/sigma, inlier votes with small predicted sigma start with more say), normalized to sum to 1 per crop. Run 3 rounds: current weighted mean (u*, v*) = sum(w_i * (u_i, v_i)); residual r_i = sqrt((u_i-u*)^2 + (v_i-v*)^2); Geman-McClure reweight w_i_new = w_i * (self.irls_scale**2 / (self.irls_scale**2 + r_i**2)**2); renormalize w_i_new to sum to 1; recompute weighted mean. All operations pure tensor ops (no argmax/data-dependent control flow, 3-iteration unroll), so the module stays ONNX-exportable with dynamo=False exactly as export_onnx already does. Final (u, v) = the last round's weighted mean.
- Confidence: from the final round's weights, compute effective sample size ess = 1 / sum(w_i^2) (normalized by dividing by 1024, so it's a 0-1 'how concentrated' signal) and the final weighted residual spread sqrt(sum(w_i * r_i^2)); feed [ess, spread, and the final round's mean log_sigma across votes] (all detached) through a small MLP (Linear(3,32)+ReLU+Linear(32,1)) into a sigmoid, minus the existing conf_shift buffer -- keep the conf_shift calibration mechanism and its buffer exactly as today so train.py's calibrate_conf_shift needs no changes beyond what's noted below.
- forward(x, return_logits=False): return torch.cat([u, v, conf], dim=1) as today; when return_logits=True, return (out, per_vote_predictions) where per_vote_predictions is the raw 1,024 x 3 (u,v,log_sigma) tensor per crop (batched), needed by the new loss_fn.
- loss_fn(pred, per_vote, target_uv, warmup_t: float) signature change (warmup_t in [0,1], 0=full warmup/plain-L2 phase, 1=full curriculum on) -- train.py passes this each step. During warmup (interpolate smoothly, e.g. multiply the NLL-minus-L2 delta and confidence-BCE term by warmup_t itself, so it's a smooth ramp rather than a hard switch at 15%): loss = consensus_L2 + mean_per_vote_L2 + warmup_t * (heteroscedastic_NLL_extra_term + 0.3 * confidence_BCE), where heteroscedastic_NLL_extra_term is the standard per-vote NLL (0.5*log_sigma + 0.5*(err/sigma)^2 per vote, averaged) MINUS the plain L2 already counted, so at warmup_t=0 the loss is pure L2 on votes+consensus and at warmup_t=1 it's the full heteroscedastic objective. Keep the confidence BCE target definition (good = consensus coord_err.sqrt() < GOOD_ERR_UV) exactly as today.

model/train.py:
- Delete compute_cell_weights (GRID_K-based); add compute_location_weights(area, data_dir, meta, crops) operating directly on the `crops` list from list_crops: for each crop location, compute a small descriptor (mean RGB + luminance std) from a local patch of reference.tif around (cx, cy) sized to roughly one grid cell's ground footprint, then nearest-DISTANT-location search (exclude locations within NEIGHBOR_EXCLUDE_R grid-cells-equivalent of ground distance) using the same chunked |a-b|^2 = |a|^2+|b|^2-2a.b trick exp-55's implementation used to keep it O(N) memory instead of a naive O(N^2) matrix, since Berlin has ~45k train locations. Blend with CONFUSABILITY_ALPHA exactly as today's crop_probs blend does, just computed over the raw crop list index space directly instead of via a grid-cell lookup.
- Add IRLS_SCALE_START/IRLS_SCALE_END and a WARMUP_FRAC = 0.15 module constant. In train_area's step loop, compute progress = global_step / total_steps once total_steps is known (as today); each step before the forward pass, set model.irls_scale = torch.tensor(IRLS_SCALE_START * (IRLS_SCALE_END/IRLS_SCALE_START) ** min(progress / max(WARMUP_FRAC, 1e-6), 1.0)) so the scale finishes annealing to IRLS_SCALE_END exactly at the end of the warmup fraction and stays there after (do NOT re-widen it later); compute warmup_t = min(progress / WARMUP_FRAC, 1.0) and pass it to loss_fn. After the epoch loop, explicitly fix model.irls_scale to IRLS_SCALE_END before calibrate_conf_shift and export, so the exported ONNX graph has a constant (not a training-time-varying) scale baked in.
- Bump EPOCH_MULT from 3 to 6 (module constant, one-line change) -- this is the concrete 'cash in the real budget' lever independent of whatever --epochs the harness passes this run.
- Remove the trunk/head LR param-group split (there is no pretrained trunk this round): single Adam optimizer over all model.parameters() at 1e-3, same CosineAnnealingLR to zero over total_steps.
- Update the info dict's 'init' field to 'from-scratch (no pretrained trunk)' and keep logging n_train_crops, epochs, total_epochs_run, epoch_mult, lr_schedule, confusability_alpha (rename cell_weight_ratio_p90_p10 to location_weight_ratio_p90_p10 computed the same way over the new weights) plus new fields irls_scale_start/irls_scale_end/warmup_frac for lineage.
- Everything else (prepare_realizations, sample_epoch's per-epoch fresh-draw structure, calibrate_conf_shift's mechanism) stays as today, just fed by compute_location_weights' crop_probs instead of compute_cell_weights' cell_w[crop_cell] lookup.
